title: Midday infra scrapbook — workbench list
content:
MIDDAY SCRAPBOOK — quick brain dump and tactical list

Context: quick personal notes while triaging capacity and a noisy node in us-west-2. Not polished — mostly reminders and short commands I might need later.

Top of mind (ordered):
- Clear the 2x pending Dedicated reservations (tickets: JIRA-4567). Need to confirm whether to flake to burst-pool or delay rollout.
- Investigate intermittent NVLink errors on rack-14 node-gp2-11 (observed 03/12 10:41 & 11:22).
- Confirm egress shaping rule that started at 09:05 — caused brief API timeout for hosted inference.

Immediate TODOs (today):
[ ] Quick repro of NVLink fail: run stress small model on gp2-11 during low-traffic window (after 17:00). Log dmesg + nvidia-smi -q.
[ ] Add temporary autoscale override for dedicated-pool-alpha: +4 gpus for next 4 hours.
[ ] File a brief postmortem note if node reboots again (collect timestamps + kernel messages).
[ ] Ping SRE on rotation to confirm egress shaping change origin (slack: #sre-network).

Commands & snippets I keep reusing:
- Check GPUs quickly: sudo -u infra/bin/nvidia-smi -a | sed -n '1,120p'
- Tail recent kernel logs from node: ssh root@gp2-11 'journalctl -k -n 300 --no-pager'
- List pods on node: kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gp2-11 -n redwood-serving
- Drain / Cordon (if needed): kubectl cordon gp2-11 && kubectl drain gp2-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n redwood-serving
- Quick capacity calc: current-dedicated-gpu = 86; expected-req-next-3h = 98; shortfall = 12 -> request burst +4 now, plan schedule for +8 in next 24h.

Observations & notes:
- gp2-11: small NVLink ECC errors; not trending but spikes after heavy KV-cache warmups. Possible thermal throttling? fans slightly louder.
- Egress shaping at 09:05 coincided with a Canaries deploy from product/hosted-api (deploy-2026-03-12_09_02). Might be related; check rollout config.
- Queue depth on torque-queue increased between 08:45–09:20 by ~27%. Hypothesis: a spike in short-running waveform evals (see ticket GH-PR-239 for ci-run changes).

Decisions to make (short):
- If gp2-11 shows another ECC spike within 12h -> schedule maintenance and move pods to gp2-12/gp2-13.
- Allow burst autoscale for dedicated-pool-alpha for next 12 hours if latency < 150ms on warmups.
- If egress shaping was intentional by network, request exception for inference-control-plane during business hours.

Handoff snippet for evening shift (to drop into handoff doc):
- What I did: created temporary autoscale +4 for dedicated-pool-alpha, ran quick health-checks on gp2-11, left node cordon as False (not drained).
- What to watch: NVLink ECC logs (dmesg) and pod restarts on gp2-11. If more than 2 restarts in 30m -> cordon+drain and open escalation with HW.
- Contact: Jamal Ortiz (pager) for urgent reboots; Meera for capacity adjustments. Links: JIRA-4567, GH-PR-239.

Loose thoughts / brainstorm fragments:
- Could we add a lifecycle policy to automatically migrate hot-KV pods off nodes with NVLink errors? Maybe a toleration/key we write to nodes when health-check fails > 2 times in 1 hour.
- Consider short-lived pre-warm workers in different AZs to reduce cross-AZ NVLink pressure during cache-warms.

Notes to self (short):
- remember to capture timestamped screenshots of console latency spikes before changing autoscale.
- If draining gp2-11, set graceful period to 60s for grpc services.

Small checklist to commit before EOD:
- [ ] Upload dmesg + nvidia-smi dump to JIRA-4567
- [ ] Add follow-up card to backlog: "node-health: auto-migrate hot-KV pods" (low priority, spike frequency needed)
- [ ] Slack short note to #platform-ops summarizing autoscale tweak and why (link to this doc)

Unresolved questions:
- Why did the egress shaping trigger exactly at 09:05? human or automated policy? (ask #sre-network)
- Are we hitting any pending capacity-based rate limits on the Dedicated API that would explain the surge?

End of scrap — if I reboot gp2-11 later, add reboot marker here with time + reason.

-- Asha K.
